cards.text: Meet Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The word of the LORD comes to him, and God calls him Son of man. God says the people around Ezekiel have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear.

cards.question: God says these people have eyes to see and ears to hear, but they don't see or hear. What reason does God give?

cards.text: So God's plan isn't a sermon. It's a one-man SHOW: pack your bags and, in broad daylight, set out from your place to another while they watch.

cards.question: Ezekiel's packing his bags in front of everybody. What kind of trip is God telling him to act out?
God says the people are sure to understand the moment they see Ezekiel's bags come out.

cards.text: God's orders: bring the bags out by day, then in the evening go out like someone going into exile. And the front door is RIGHT THERE, but with everybody watching, God tells Ezekiel to dig through the wall and carry his things out through it.

cards.question: At dusk, with his bags on his shoulder, God tells Ezekiel to cover his face. Why?

answers.text: So he cannot see the land

cards.question: God explains what all this acting is for. He has made Ezekiel a ___ to the house of Israel.
Strange orders and all, Ezekiel does exactly as God commanded him.

cards.text: Ezekiel digs through the wall by hand and heads out at dusk with his bags on his shoulder, while everybody watches. Friend, if my neighbor tunneled out of his own house with a suitcase, I'm skipping the contractor and calling the GROUP CHAT.

The next morning, the word of the LORD comes, and God brings up the question the rebellious house asked Ezekiel: 'What are you doing?' Fair question, and I'd have asked it while he was still elbow-deep in the wall.

cards.question: God gives Ezekiel the answer to tell them. Who does this burden concern?

answers.text: The prince in Jerusalem and the people there
The exiles living right there with Ezekiel
The kings of the nations around Israel

cards.question: Ezekiel is to tell them he is a sign. What happened to him will be done to them, and they will go into exile as ___.

cards.text: The one ruling in Jerusalem is Zedekiah, king of Judah (2 Kings 24:17-18), and God says the prince will lift his bags to his shoulder at dusk and go out, they'll dig through the wall to bring him out, and he'll cover his face so he can't see the land. Ezekiel was the rehearsal, and THIS is opening night.

cards.question: The prince slips out with his face covered. What does God say He will spread over him?
God says the prince will be brought to Babylon and will see it with his own eyes.

cards.text: The prince will die there, in Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans.
His attendants and troops get scattered to every wind, with a sword chasing after them. When God disperses them among the nations, they will know that He is the LORD.

cards.question: God says He will spare a few of them from sword and famine and plague. Why?

answers.text: So they can recount their abominations among the nations
So they can rebuild the ruined altars of Jerusalem
So they can bring offerings to the house of the LORD

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again. No digging this time, just a meal.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel how to eat his bread and drink his water. How is he supposed to do it?

cards.text: Then Ezekiel tells the people of the land what it means. The people in Jerusalem and the land of Israel will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dread.

cards.question: God says the land of Israel will be stripped of everything in it because of the ___ of all who dwell in it.
God says the cities will stay standing even while the land suffers.

cards.text: Again the word of the LORD comes, this time about a proverb people have in the land of Israel: 'The days go by, and every vision fails.'

cards.question: When the people say every vision fails, what do they mean?

answers.text: The visions are hard to understand

cards.question: God hears Israel's proverb about failing visions and says He'll let it keep spreading.

cards.text: In its place, God gives them a new line: 'The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled.' That old proverb was the snooze button, friend, and God just told them the alarm is ringing NOW.

cards.question: God says false visions and flattering divinations will keep showing up in the house of Israel.
God says whatever word He speaks will be fulfilled without ___.
God tells the rebellious house when He'll bring His message to pass. When?

cards.text: Then a second saying: 'The vision that he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about the distant future.' That's the bill on the counter, friend. Oh, it's real. It's just FUTURE ME's problem.

cards.question: This second saying claims Ezekiel's visions will never happen at all.
What is God's answer to the saying that Ezekiel's vision is for the distant future?

answers.text: None of His words will be delayed any longer
The vision really is for many years from now
He will send another prophet before it comes

cards.text: Snooze button or Future Me, God gives the same answer: 'The message I speak will be fulfilled.' When He says it, you can set your timer by it.
